title: Restore the complete desktop profile under its original local account
context: A valid same-user desktop profile stopped opening when relocated. The native host derived the profile ID from its canonical directory, and the SQLite database required the original ID. A database copied by itself into another profile is already rejected.
decision: After successful native open, atomically publish a versioned private anchor beside the database. The anchor carries the stable profile ID and the verified OS account fingerprint. A new database gets a random identity component and retains the original path digest for recovery if startup ends before the anchor is installed. Existing IDs remain stable. Serialize startup admission and reject damaged journal sets and shared Windows file handles before SQLite.
authority: ADR 0007 delegates this software implementation and review repair. ADR 0011 governs local identity and disclosure. M5-005 owns the replacement software evidence and M5-001 owns packaged recovery qualification. The earlier candidate remains recoverable on its original branch.

alternatives.option: Adopt the profile ID from any private database at the new path.
alternatives.reason: A copied database alone could replace the active profile identity and its credential namespace.

alternatives.option: Rewrite the database identity and dependent records at the new path.
alternatives.reason: This would require rewriting attribution and identity-indexed state and would risk disconnecting current entitlements.

consequences: First open a pre-anchor profile through a native workspace action at its original location. Close all writers and retain the whole private workspace directory. If a legacy directory moved before its first registration, put it back at the original path for that open.

Restore into a vacant destination under the same account and preserve restrictive ownership and permissions. Preserve the original directory or backup until the restored profile has opened. A missing database, incompatible database, copied database alone or wrong account cannot claim the saved identity.

The anchor changes neither the SQLite format nor the grant records. Database tombstones and provenance remain attached to their original identity. Live folder access and policy grants still expire with their session. The OS manages existing credentials behind their original profile namespace.

An older reader can reopen a compatible legacy database at its original path. Use a reader that understands the new identity for newly created profiles. Recovery retains the original database and journals while a damaged or shared profile is refused.
revisit_when: The product qualifies a cross-account or cross-machine transfer, adds a native backup entry, or changes how platform-owned profile identities are established.
